tests.what: Apply SAVE10 via POST /api/checkout on a known subtotal and assert order.discount equals 10% of subtotal (rounded to cents) and total equals subtotal + tax - discount
Apply SAVE10 on a multi-item cart with non-round prices and assert discount rounds to cents correctly and appears in the order response
Assert tax remains 8% of the subtotal (not discounted subtotal) when SAVE10 is applied
Via UI (#/cart with data-testid=checkout-button, #/checkout order-total), assert SAVE10 reduces the displayed total by exactly 10% of the cart subtotal

plan.reason: Discount math with cent rounding is a classic seeded-bug target and the contract's 'capped at the subtotal' clause is unreachable for a 10% rate, so rounding/total-composition checks are essential.

proposal.evidence: Line 71: Expected 392.7 (10% of the 3927.00 subtotal) but received 10 — the server returned a flat $10 off instead of 10% of the subtotal. The subtotal assertion at line 69 passed, so the test's expected math matches REQ-CHK-02 ('SAVE10 takes 10% off the subtotal'); the app's discount implementation is wrong. Per rules, no fix is proposed for a product bug.

evidence: Deterministic failure: 3/3 clean-code attempts failed, ruling out flakiness.
Received discount = 10 vs expected = 392.7: the implementation behaves like a flat $10 off (SAVE10 read as '$10') instead of 10% of the subtotal, directly contradicting REQ-CHK-02.
The subtotal assertion (line 69) passed before failing at the discount assertion (line 71), so the mismatch is isolated to the discount calculation, not setup or test data.
The test's expected value is consistent with the requirement (10% of a 3927 subtotal = 392.7, rounded to the cent), so the expectation is not the defect.
proposal.missing: The checkout/discount implementation (or order API payload/trace) confirming the code computes discount as a flat 10 rather than 10% would fully confirm; conversely, authoritative spec wording defining SAVE10 as a fixed $10 off would flip this to test-bug.
